name: showreel-19-numbers

voice.text: Why do your numbers wiggle when they change? Each digit has its own width. A one is narrow, a zero is wide. So every tick, the line shifts. The fix: font variant numeric, tabular nums. Now every digit takes the same width. Timers, prices and scores hold still.

caption:
Why do your numbers wiggle when they change? ⏱️

Most fonts give each digit its own width: a 1 is narrow, a 0 is wide. So a live timer, price or score shifts sideways every time a digit changes. Add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and every digit takes the same width, so the number holds still. One line of CSS, in every major browser. (It uses the font's tabular figures, so the font needs them; most UI fonts have them.)
Save it for your next dashboard, or send it to whoever builds your UI.

sources.note: MDN font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums activates figures that are all the same size (OpenType tnum)
font-variant-numeric: Chrome 52, Firefox 34, Safari 9.1; works only if the font has tabular figures

tip.title: Why do your numbers wiggle when they change?
tip.why: Most fonts use proportional digits: a 1 is narrower than a 0, so a live timer, price or score shifts sideways whenever a digit changes. font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums switches to the font's tabular figures, where every digit has the same width, so the number holds still. The font needs tabular figures (OpenType tnum); most UI fonts have them.
